full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of her title to the suit land and for khas possession thereof by evicting the defendants. The case of the plaintiff in brief is like this:— The plaintiff purchased the raiyati jote with a jama of Rs.23/- recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 840 from Rahim Baksha Sarkar and others by a registered deed of sale dated 11th June, 1941, and by the said deed the plaintiff also acquired the right to sue the under raiyat for recovery of arrear rent. This raiyats jote comprised of 7.89 acres of land. Under this raiyati jote an under raiyati with a jama of Rs. 26-4 annas in respect of 5.48 acres of land was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 841 which was held by Ashatulla Sarkar and others. The plaintiff purchased the right of recovery of arrear rent in respect of this under raiyati. Thereafter the plaintiff obtained a rent decree against the under raiyats Ashatulla Sarkar and others and by executing the rent decree purchased the under raiyati interest in auction sale held on 2nd June, 1953 in Rent Execution case No.1236 of 1952 and took delivery of possession on 2nd June, 1953. Further case of the plaintiff is that after taking delivery of possession of the auction purchased land through Court, the plaintiff's husband went to the suit land measuring 2.24 acres of land appertaining to the said under raiyati jama for cultivation but the defendant resisted. However, they took time to remove their huts from the suit lands but ultimately refused to vacate the same. In this context the plaintiff's further case is that the defendants has no valid interest in the land inasmuch as if the under raiyats, namely Ashatullah Sarkar and others settled any land with the defendants creating a under raiyat of the second or third degree, it is not binding upon the plaintiff as it was done without the consent of the plaintiff or his predecessor-in-interest. 

 3. The suit was resisted by defendants 1,7 and 8 by filing a joint written statement but the defendant No.1 Juran Sheikh alone contested the suit at the trial. In the written statement it was contended, inter alia, that Bonde Ali Sheikh predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos.1 and 7 to 16 had been in possession of the suit land with their homestead thereon for about 40 years as a tenant under the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff; and the under raiyati interest recorded in C.S. 841 was at first held by Mebarulla Sheikh at a jama of Rs. 22/- under Rabim Baksh and others. Meharulla Sheikh sold his interest to Baharullah Bepari and the latter held the under raiyati at a jama of Rs.26-4 annas; and the Baharullah Bepari died leaving four sons Ashatulla and three others, five daughters, two widows and one of the daughters Subjan died leaving Chotomai as her heir:— and that Chotomai bibi also died leaving her heir Dholi Mai but she was not made a party. Therefore, the decree obtained in the rent suit was not rent decree and consequently the alleged rent sale did not affect the defendants. It was further contended by the defendants that under the under raiyati recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 841 standing in the name of Ashatultah Sarkar and others there are several sub-leases or under raiyati interests of second and third degree recorded in C.S. Khatian Nos. 844, 847 and 843. The under raiyati in respect of 1.84 acres recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 848 was held by Bonde Ali Sheikh and Juran Sheikh under Meharullah at a jama of Rs. 15/- under a registered patta dated the 13th November, 1919, corresponding to 27th Kartic 1326 B.S. Jama was enhanced to Rs.15.5 annas after Bahrulla purchased the under raiyati interest from Meharulla when Juran Sheikh and Bonde Ali Sheikh executed a registered kabuliyat dated 26th November, 1927 corresponding 10th Agrabayan, 1334 B.S. for cultivation and residential purpose. Thus the under raiyati interest held by the defendants under Baharulla has neither been affected by the alleged rent sale nor the plaintiff on the basis of that rent sale is entitled to get khas possession of the land by evicting the defendants. The under raiyati in respect of 40 acre recorded in C.S. Khatian No.847 was held only by Bonde Ali Sheikh at a jama of Rs. 4-8 annas under Khalil Mahmud Mondal whose interest has been recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 844 and so long the interest of Khalil Mahmud is not made khas, the subordinate interest of the defendants also cannot be made khas and that in any view of the matter the interest of the defendants being protected under the law, the plaintiff cannot get khas possession by evicting the defendants, contended that the plaintiff cannot have a decree for khas possession, inasmuch as, with the consent of the landlords, namely, Rahim Baksha and others the under raiyaties were created, and as such the transfer being valid in law, and also the defendants and their predecessor-in-interest having their homestead in the suit land appertaining to the said under raiyati interest, the plaintiff cannot get khas possession by evicting the defendants, because the interest of the defendants in suit land is protected. 

 4. The following issues were framed for trial of the suit:- (1) Had the plaintiff any right, title and interest in the suit land? Is the plaintiff entitled to get khas possession of demolishing the huts ? (3) To what relief is the plaintiff entitled to? 

 6. On the question as to whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree for khas possession by removing the huts of the defendants from the suit land, the learned Munsif held that the sub-leases created by the under raiyats having been done without any consent from the landlord, are not valid in law and the same were not binding on the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff, nor the same is binding upon the plaintiff. With this findings the learned Munsif decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff directing that the plaintiff do get khas possession of the suit land by evicting the defendants and removing the huts therefrom. In appeal by the defendant No.1 the decision of the learned Munsif was affirmed. The learned District Judge who heard this appeal concurred With the findings of the learned Munsif on both the points. Being aggrieved by the said decision on this second appeal was preferred. 

 7. In this second appeal the question of non joinder or misjoinder of necessary parties in the suit has not been pressed by the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant. The submissions made by the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant centered mainly round the question as to whether the under raiyati interests recorded in C.S. Khatian Nos. 848 and 847 are valid in law and whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree for ejectment of the under raiyats. It appears from the judgments of the Courts below that it was argued on behalf of the defendants that the under raiyati interests recorded in C.S. Khatian Nos. 848 and 847 and also 944 had been created before the Bengal Tenancy Act was amended in 1928 by which section 48F was incorporated along with some other sections and section 85 was omitted. Since section 48F is not applicable to the above mentioned under raiyati interest should be treated as valid in law and as such the undo raiyats cannot be treated as unauthorised trespassers in the suit land. In support of this contention reliance was placed on a decision of the Calcutta High Court, namely, Munshi Serajnl Huq Mia Vs. Abjal Mia and another reported in A.I.R. 1941 Cal. 351 same decision has been reported in 45 Calcutta Weekly Notes page 339. It appears that above noted argument of the learned Advocate did not find favour. The learned District Judge held that before the amendment of the Act in 1928 an under raiyat could create a sublease but it would not be binding upon the landlord because the under raiyati interest is not transferable which was made transferable only under section 48F of the amended Act 1928 with the consent of the landlord, and as such the sub-leases created by Baharulla and others are not binding upon the plaintiff and since the plaintiff has auction purchased the under raiyati of first decree the sub-leases created in favour of the defendants and their predecessor-in-interest, have ceased to exist and the plaintiff is entitled to get khas possession of the land by removing the defendants therefrom. 

 13. There is yet another material question involved in this case but it has been totally ignored by the Courts below. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants points out that the defendants pleaded that after acquisition of the rent-receiving-interest the under raiyats have become tenants under the Government and accordingly Khatians have been prepared in favour of the tenants and as such the plaintiff's suit for khas possession by evicting such tenants is liable to be dismissed. On examination of the materials on record it appears that the submissions of the learned Advocate has substance. After the defendants have become tenants direct under the Government they are not liable to be ejected by the plaintiff. The Courts below erred in decreeing the suit for ejectment totally ignoring that the defendants are now tenant under the Government and they cannot be ejected at the instance of the plaintiff who claims to have purchased the superior interest.
